Chloe — drafting notes below for the bridge letter and hosting statement. Pulling from our Private/Hosted product docs: 

1) SOC 2: our latest Type II period covers 2024-07-01 through 2025-06-30; auditor: Graystone LLP. We can provide the redacted report and a bridge letter that: (a) summarizes the controls tested in the last Type II; (b) explains that continuous controls coverage is materially unchanged since the report period; and (c) provides a timeline for when the next Type II will be issued (planned Q4 2026). Recommended phrasing: "Redwood Inference has maintained the described system of controls since the test period and intends to complete the forthcoming Type II audit in Q4 2026; where gaps exist, compensating controls (detailed below) are in place."

2) Hosting boundary: for Hosted customers the data plane (model inputs/outputs, storage) can be pinned to cloud regions (we have UK region availability) but our control plane (orchestration/management) for Hosted is presently located in EU and US clusters for resilience. For Dedicated and Private deployments the control plane can be customer-managed or restricted to the customer's VPC/region (Private deployments: control plane components can be deployed inside the customer's VPC; keys are customer-managed if requested).

3) KMS: for Private deployments customers can bring their own KMS (BYOK). For Dedicated we offer options for customer-managed keys via HSM integrations; Hosted customers use Redwood-managed KMS but we can provide key separation assurances and role-based access logs.

4) Attachments to include: SOC2_TypeII_2025-06_Redwood.pdf (redacted), draft Bridge_Letter_GreenBank_20260907.pdf, KMS_Controls_Summary.txt.

Action for you: send the set with a short cover note answering Alice's control-plane question (i.e., Hosted: metadata may cross borders; Private: control plane stays in-customer region). I'll sign off on the bridge language and we should propose a DocuSign DPA link.
